where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-21 and DM-ACU-ROUTE-21B (K06 rewrite); DM-ACU-ROUTE-19, -01 stop conditions
finding: Regression from K06. The rewrite dropped 'any glucose 11.1 or more / HI' from ROUTE-21's diabetes context (ROUTE-21B was built the same way), while ROUTE-19 ('raised glucose with vomiting: test ketones') and ROUTE-01 still stand down as soon as any ketone result exists. A person not yet known to have diabetes, with a high glucose, vomiting and intermediate ketones, now reaches nothing. Evaluator: L-A1 new adult, district, meter 28, vomiting, urine ketones 1+ -> only DM-SUS-INCID-01 routine ('repeat on another day'), caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture; before the K fixes (base_r4) -> ROUTE-21 same_day + REFER-GLU-02 same_day. Grid: adult, no diabetes info, vomiting, glucose 15 or 28 x urine trace / 1+ / bohb 1.0 -> 6 of 6 cells silent (all fired same_day before K06).
why: New-onset ketosis-prone diabetes and type 1 presenting in adulthood are common in Uganda; vomiting with ketonuria and a glucose of 28 is the early DKA picture. Rule 4 and rule 8: the only text on screen tells the clinician to repeat the test another day. ROUTE-02/22/30 already accept a raised glucose as diabetes context; 21/21B are the odd ones out.
fix: Give ROUTE-21 and ROUTE-21B the same context list as ROUTE-02/22/30 (DM_CONTEXT: known, type 1, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2, HI, or glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-DKA-GLU). Add vignette L-A1 (expect ROUTE-21 same_day). Add the build check R5 asked for under K01: every stop condition that names another rule must imply that rule's criterion for the same patient (it would have caught this and L02).

where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 notWhen acu_glu18_signs (K08) vs DM-ACU-ROUTE-04 / -25 sign lists
finding: Regression from K08. ROUTE-01 ('glucose 18 or more: test ketones today') now stands down on deep breathing, ACETONE BREATH, dehydration or drowsiness because 'an interrupting rule applies'. For children no interrupting rule reads acetone: ROUTE-04's list is vomiting, pain, deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness; ROUTE-25's is deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness; ROUTE-24 (which reads acetone) is adult-only. Evaluator: L-C12 8-year-old, known type 1 on insulin, meter 20, acetone on the breath -> NOTHING (base_r4: ROUTE-01 same_day). L-C12b 8-year-old, no diabetes info, meter 20, acetone -> PAED-03 same_day only (base_r4: + ROUTE-01).
why: Ketotic breath with a glucose of 20 in a child with type 1 is ketoacidosis until shown otherwise (NICE NG18 lists it among DKA features). The K08 stop silenced the one prompt that was left. Rule 4.
fix: Add acetone_breath to ROUTE-04's and ROUTE-25's sign lists (NICE NG18, the source behind REF-DM-ACU-PAED-DKA), or limit ROUTE-01's stop to the signs that an interrupt for the same age band actually reads. Vignette L-C12.

finding: Severe pre-eclampsia below 160/110 is never routed, and a negative strip silences it. UCG-PE-02 (the pack's own research row) defines severe pre-eclampsia as 160/110 with proteinuria 'OR any degree of hypertension with evidence of organ dysfunction'; UCG-HTN-03 lists eclampsia/pre-eclampsia as a hypertensive emergency. The new hypertensive_organ_damage finding (K10) is read only by ROUTE-29, which needs >180/110 and is now stopped by 'pregnant' (K08); ROUTE-28 reads BP only; ROUTE-27 is cleared by a negative urine protein (K11). Evaluator: L-B5 pregnant 34 weeks, 150/100, hypertensive_organ_damage (seizures / visual loss / confusion) -> ROUTE-27 same_day 'urine protein today'. L-B7 same with urine protein neg -> NOTHING. L-B5x 34 weeks, 150/100, drowsy -> ROUTE-27 same_day only.
why: Seizures, visual loss or a falling conscious level in a hypertensive pregnant woman is eclampsia or imminent eclampsia: a maternal-death emergency at any BP above 140/90. Rule 4; the source the pack cites says so.
fix: Add an immediate arm to ROUTE-28 (or a new rule): pregnant or within REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM weeks postpartum, BP >= REF-DM-PREG-BP-SBP/DBP, with hypertensive_organ_damage or mental_status drowsy or worse, sourced to UCG-PE-02 and UCG-HTN-03. ROUTE-27's 'protein negative' stop must not apply when organ damage or drowsiness is recorded. Vignettes L-B5, L-B7, L-B5x.

finding: The rules still disagree on who 'has diabetes'. K01 made type 1 recorded, insulin and SGLT2 count as diabetes in ROUTE-02/22/24/30 and K05 built ROUTE-32 on known/type 1/insulin, but ROUTE-25 (child, signs) reads only dm_status == known and ROUTE-20 (drowsy, no glucose) reads known/insulin/SU. Evaluator: L-C1 8-year-old, insulin on the list, status blank, deep rapid breathing, glucose 7 -> NOTHING. L-C2 8-year-old, type 1 recorded, status blank, drowsy, glucose 7 -> ROUTE-09 same_day only. Grid: child and adolescent, insulin-listed or type-1-recorded with status blank, Kussmaul, glucose 7, any ketone below 3.0 -> 28 cells with no interrupt (12 with nothing at all). Adult type 1 recorded, status blank, drowsy, no glucose -> ROUTE-09 same_day (7 cells); L-S3 SGLT2 listed, status blank, drowsy, no glucose -> nothing.
why: A child on insulin with Kussmaul breathing has ketoacidosis until shown otherwise whatever the glucose (NICE NG18: in known diabetes suspect DKA even with a normal glucose; partially treated DKA). Relatives often bring the insulin pen while the status box stays blank. Rule 4.
fix: Define one diabetes-context list in k_review (known, type 1 recorded, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2 inhibitor) and use it in ROUTE-13, -20, -23, -25, -32 and ROUTE-07's context, as K01 did for 02/22/24/30. Vignettes L-C1, L-C2, L-S3.

finding: Inverse escalation: the sicker insulin or SGLT2 user gets less. ROUTE-23 ('on insulin, vomiting: ketones today') stands down on dehydration or drowsiness because 'an interrupting rule applies', but below a glucose of 11.1 no interrupt reads either sign (ROUTE-11 needs 11.1; ROUTE-24 reads only deep breathing and acetone). ROUTE-03 (SGLT2) reads vomiting, pain, deep breathing and acute illness, but not drowsiness or dehydration. Evaluator: L-A6 type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7 -> ROUTE-23 same_day; L-A4 same + dehydrated -> NOTHING; L-A5 same + drowsy -> NOTHING (identical before the K fixes). L-S1 type 2 on an SGLT2 inhibitor, drowsy, glucose 8 -> NOTHING (only routine steps).
why: Drowsiness and dehydration are late features of ketoacidosis; at a near-normal glucose they are exactly the euglycaemic and partly treated DKA the pack's notes describe (2024 hyperglycaemic-crises consensus behind REF-DM-ACU-DKA-BOHB: prior diabetes qualifies at any glucose). Rule 4.
fix: ROUTE-23's sign stop: deep breathing and acetone only (what ROUTE-24 reads). Add dehydration and drowsiness to ROUTE-24's sign list for insulin/SGLT2/type 1 users at any glucose (or a new interrupt 'glucose below 11.1 with these signs: ketones now'), and add dehydration and drowsiness to ROUTE-03's 'any', sourced to the consensus and REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN; CSO signature under D-DM-37. Vignettes L-A4, L-A5, L-S1.

where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-23 notWhen acu_insulin_sick_done, DM-ACU-ROUTE-32 notWhen acu_paed_known_sick_done
finding: K02's principle (a urine strip never stands down a ketone prompt) was applied to the SGLT2 rule only. A vomiting child on insulin with a normal glucose and one negative strip reaches nothing. Evaluator: L-C4 8-year-old type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7, urine ketones neg -> only caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture; L-C4b without the strip -> ROUTE-23 same_day.
why: REF-DM-VAL-URINE-KETONE (strips underestimate early) applies to insulin deficiency as much as to SGLT2. ISPAD sick-day guidance: a vomiting child with diabetes needs blood ketones and contact with the diabetes team. Referral is in scope under rule 3.
fix: ROUTE-23: clear on bohb < REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW only (as K02 did for ROUTE-03); with a urine result only, keep it (same_day). Vignette L-C4.

finding: The K fixes added 290 double-interrupt cells to the grid (1,155 cells with two or more 'immediate' items; 865 existed before; up to 5 immediates in one cell). New pairs and their cause: ROUTE-03 with 24/11/14/30/25/04/32 (K02 narrowed 03's stop to rule 02 only; K01 put SGLT2 in 24) - L-S2 SGLT2, Kussmaul, glucose 8 -> 03 + 24; K02d SGLT2, vomiting, bohb 2.0 -> 03 + 30. ROUTE-30 with 04/32/07/14 (no stops) - child type 1, vomiting, glucose 14, bohb 2.0 -> 04 + 30. ROUTE-31 with 07: A10 / L-H1 known diabetes, blank list, drowsy, 3.5 -> 07 + 31, because 31's stop is labelled 'or known diabetes without a medicine list that excludes them' but does not test dm_status (rule 10 too). ROUTE-28 + 29: L-B4 3 weeks postpartum, 200/120, organ damage -> both (29's K08 stop reads 'pregnant' only; K11 extended 28 to postpartum). ROUTE-32 with 02/14/04. Pre-existing pairs still present: 02+04 (96 cells), 04+14 (child HI), 20+25 and 07+25 (70 each), 02+14.
why: Rule 9 and the pack's own 'one interrupt per event' principle (J09, K08).
fix: ROUTE-03 notWhen the criteria of 11, 14, 24, 30 (and 04/25/32 for children); ROUTE-30 notWhen 04, 25, 32; ROUTE-31's r07 stop: add KNOWN() so it matches its label; ROUTE-29 notWhen postpartum_weeks <= REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM; ROUTE-32 notWhen ketones 2+ / bohb >= 3.0. Turn the grid (phase-1/r6/grid.py) into a build check: no cell may carry two 'immediate' items from the same condition family.

finding: A meter reading of HI or LO is not 'a glucose on record': GLU_REC lists the numeric fields only. Rules then say 'no glucose on record: capillary glucose now' right after the meter has read HI or LO. Evaluator: L-C11 14-year-old type 1, vomiting, meter HI -> ROUTE-04, -14 and -32 immediate ('no glucose on record'), plus ROUTE-01 and -23 same_day (five items). Adult on insulin, drowsy, meter LO -> ROUTE-06 + ROUTE-20 'no glucose on record: capillary glucose now'. Adult type 2, vomiting, meter HI -> ROUTE-13 'no glucose on record' + ROUTE-14. ROUTE-32 (new, K05) inherits it.
why: Rule 10 (the display contradicts the record) and rule 9; at a meter-only site HI/LO is the reading.
fix: Add P('glucose_meter_extreme','recorded') to GLU_REC. Vignette L-C11 (expect one interrupt).

where: 40-stratify.json tgt_hba1c_general notWhen tgt_general_older (K13); tgt_hba1c_older_healthy notWhen tier_not_any
finding: Regression from K13: an older adult whose clinician has agreed the GENERAL tier gets no HbA1c target at all. tgt_hba1c_general now stands down at 65 or over, and the older-adult target stands down whenever any tier is agreed. Evaluator: 72-year-old type 2, tier 'general', HbA1c 7.3 -> targets fpg/ppg/bp only (base_r4: tgt_hba1c_general). Also (pre-existing): tier 'tight' or 'avoid_symptoms' -> no HbA1c target at any age.
why: The agreed target is the one the clinician needs on screen (R5 K13's own reason); the agreed tier now erases it.
fix: tgt_hba1c_general: replace the age stop with when = known AND any(age < REF-DM-CTRL-OLDER-AGE, tier == general). Decide what 'tight' and 'avoid_symptoms' propose (ADA SOC section 6/13 under D-DM-40) or state that they propose none. Vignette: 72, tier general -> tgt_hba1c_general.

finding: K10 is partly fixed. The new hypertensive_organ_damage box interrupts, but hypertensive_symptoms still reads 'headache, breathlessness, blurred vision, confusion, nausea or vomiting, or little urine' and REFER-BP-03's display repeats the list as same-day. The same confusion or anuria is an interrupt in one box and a same-day referral in the other. Evaluator: L-B1 / J18a known type 2, 190/115 or 230/130, hypertensive_symptoms true -> REFER-BP-01 same_day only; DMV-110 with hypertensive_organ_damage -> ROUTE-29 immediate.
why: Rule 10 and rule 4: the clinician cannot know that ticking 'symptoms' for confusion does not route.
fix: Remove the UCG-HTN-03 items (confusion, visual disturbance, breathlessness, little urine) from hypertensive_symptoms and from BP-03's display; leave headache and nausea there; per UCG 2023 4.1.6.1.

where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-07 notWhen acu_hypo_l1_list_clear and display; DM-ACU-ROUTE-26 (adult only, KNOWN)
finding: Three problems in the K04 hypoglycaemia split. (a) ROUTE-07's stop says '(rule 26 applies)' but ROUTE-26 is adult-only: child and adolescent on metformin or an SGLT2 inhibitor with glucose 3.5 -> nothing (grid: 32 cells; L-C5 14-year-old type 2 on metformin, 3.5 -> nothing). (b) A recorded type is not read as diabetes: L-H13 type 2 recorded, status and list blank, 3.5 -> NOTHING. (c) ROUTE-07's display still reads 'on insulin or a sulfonylurea, or with type 1 diabetes' while its new arm fires on known diabetes alone: L-H12 metformin only, type blank, 3.6 -> ROUTE-07 immediate with that text; DMV-104 (list and type blank) asserts it.
why: (a, b) A glucose below 3.9 in a person with diabetes is ADA level 1 and needs at least a same-day response; under 16, referral is in scope (rule 3). (c) Rule 10: the display names a medicine the person is not recorded as taking.
fix: ROUTE-26: all age bands, with a referral display for children. Add dm_type_recorded in (type_2, other, unclassified, gestational) to the known-diabetes arm of ROUTE-07 and ROUTE-26 (and L04's shared list). ROUTE-07's display per arm: '... or with diabetes and no medicine list to exclude them'.

finding: ROUTE-25 says 'suspected ketoacidosis' to a hypoglycaemic child: it stands down only on a glucose above 11. Evaluator: L-C3 8-year-old type 1, drowsy, glucose 3.5 -> ROUTE-07 immediate AND ROUTE-25 immediate 'suspected ketoacidosis. Route now'; grid: child/adolescent type 2 on metformin or SGLT2, drowsy, 3.5 -> ROUTE-25 + ROUTE-31 (28 cells, new with ROUTE-31).
why: Rule 10 and rule 9: the drowsy child with a glucose of 3.5 has hypoglycaemia; a ketoacidosis label beside it invites the wrong first action.
fix: ROUTE-25 notWhen any glucose < REF-DM-HYPO-L1 or a meter LO (rules 06, 07, 31 interrupt).

where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-27, -28 (pregnancy arm insufficient); build.py run_vignette gaps
finding: A woman who could be pregnant with no answer recorded gets nothing for severe hypertension: the pregnancy atLeast is 'insufficient', rules do not report a missing answer, and no pregnancy prompt appears. Evaluator: L-B8 woman 29, pregnancy blank, 170/115 -> nothing in rules (gaps only on diagnosis sets); L-B8b same with known type 2 -> REFER-BP-01 same_day only.
why: Rule 2: the missing answer behaves as 'not pregnant'. At 170/115 the answer decides between a same-day referral and an interrupt (UCG-PE-02).
fix: When the BP arm of ROUTE-27/28 is met and pregnancy is unknown, report 'pregnant' and 'postpartum_weeks' as a named gap (as the evaluator does for criteria sets; D-DM-36's 'acute rules still run'), or a prompt to ask now. Vignette L-B8.

where: k_r5.py DISPOSITION K05/K07/K19; decisions D-DM-38; 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-GLU-02
finding: K05 is declared fixed partly through 'GLU-02 applies at any age', but K19 switched GLU-02 off in the same round. Evaluator: A15 10-year-old type 1, glucose 25, ketones neg, well -> nothing but dark: D-DM-38. L-A2 adult type 2, vomiting, glucose 28, urine neg -> nothing acute (dark). DMV-97 now asserts the silence.
why: Not a re-report of D-DM-38: the decision text does not say that, while it is unsigned, a glucose of 18 or more with negative ketones routes nowhere at any age, including a vomiting adult and a child with type 1; the CSO signs blind to that, and the disposition overstates K05.
fix: Mark K05 'fixed_in_part' and K19's consequence in D-DM-38's 'why'. For children, a non-gated arm 'glucose above REF-DM-ACU-PAED-GLU in a child with diabetes: refer to the child's diabetes team today' rests on NICE NG18/ISPAD and needs no WHO PEN choice.

finding: A negative protein strip now clears all pregnancy and postpartum BP prompts and hands follow-up to 'the hypertension pack', which does not exist in this release. Evaluator: L-B2 pregnant 34 weeks, 150/100, headache, urine protein neg -> NOTHING; L-B10 3 weeks postpartum, 145/95, protein neg -> NOTHING; B03 (28 weeks, 142/92, neg) -> nothing.
why: Gestational hypertension at 34 weeks still needs antenatal follow-up and is the precursor of pre-eclampsia (UCG-PE-04); rule 8, a district must reach a next step. Organ dysfunction without proteinuria is covered in L03.
fix: Keep a routine or same-day 'BP 140/90 or more in pregnancy or postpartum with negative protein: antenatal review' until the hypertension pack ships, citing the UCG 2023 chapter 16 section on gestational hypertension (to be added to the research table; not quoted from memory).

finding: K09 is partly fixed: when.label now says what is tested, but the display shown to the clinician still reads 'with symptoms of diabetes, a raised glucose, ketones or known diabetes: hospital now'. Evaluator: DMV-92 10-year-old with known type 1, abdominal pain, glucose 6, bohb 0.3 -> nothing fires, ROUTE-04 not met.
why: Rule 10.
fix: Make the display match the label (no 'ketones', no 'known diabetes').

finding: K16 is partly fixed. The 'recorded at this encounter' rule is now in catalog/00 semantics, but the loop meant to stamp the engine changes matches the string '"recorded"' while the spec writes '{panel, recorded}': 0 recordedScope entries in 00-engine-changes.json. The Design B manifest carries no time scope (0 hits), although the semantics text says 'Design B carries the time scope'.
why: The implementer works from the engine-change spec; every 'already recorded' stop (ROUTE-01/13/15/18/19/20/23/32) is satisfied by an old value without it.
fix: Write recordedScope explicitly on the panel-atom EC entry and assert it in the build; carry the scope into the manifest.

finding: Display still says 'Known diabetes (or on insulin or a sulfonylurea)'; the K01 label adds type 1 and SGLT2. Evaluator: L-S2 SGLT2 patient sees that text.
why: Rule 10.
fix: Display from the label.

finding: 'with high glucose or known diabetes' omits type 1, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2 (K01). Evaluator: DMV-101 (insulin, status blank) shows it.
why: Rule 10.
fix: Display from the label.

finding: Display says 'contact the diabetes team now' with urgency same_day (K03).
why: Rule 10.
fix: 'today', or urgency matching 'now'.

finding: Same-day prompt stacked under an interrupt: A19 -> ROUTE-11 + ROUTE-21; DMV-88 -> ROUTE-03 + ROUTE-21 (K08 asked for 21/22 notWhen interrupts).
why: Rule 9.
fix: notWhen the interrupting criteria.

finding: Fires with ketones already recorded, asking for 'glucose and ketones now'. Evaluator: L-C10 child type 1, vomiting, urine 3+ -> ROUTE-02 + ROUTE-32 + ROUTE-18.
why: Rule 10.
fix: Display 'glucose now' when a ketone result exists, or stop on rule 02.

finding: K23 banded the 10-year-old 'child' while K24's semantics says the child band ends before 10 years.
why: Vignettes must test what the pack states.
fix: Band DMV-92 'adolescent' or correct the semantics line.

finding: Title says 'with headache'; no headache recorded.
why: Vignette accuracy.
fix: Record hypertensive_symptoms or retitle.

finding: Accepts ROUTE-26 same_day 'recheck today' alongside the ROUTE-31 interrupt (observed: both fire).
why: Rule 9.
fix: ROUTE-26 notWhen ROUTE-31's criterion; assert silent.

finding: K12 stops on pregnant==true only; with pregnancy unanswered it still says 'repeat fasting on another day'. Evaluator: A16b woman 30, fasting meter 6.3, pregnancy blank -> INCID-04 routine.
why: Rule 2.
fix: Show 'pregnant' as a named gap with the prompt.

finding: The 'HbA1c cannot be used' gap exists only in the reference evaluator (B01/B01b/DMV-95 -> gap hba1c, RX-11 silent); the catalog item has no arm or display for it, so an engine reading the catalog shows nothing.
why: Rule 10 / implementability.
fix: Add the arm R5 described (display + needsBeforeActing), or an EC entry requiring the engine to show blocked gaps.

finding: gestation_weeks is still unread; the display gives both readings (pre-eclampsia from 20 weeks, chronic hypertension before) for every patient. L-B9 12 weeks, 142/92, protein 1+ -> same text.
why: Rule 10.
fix: Branch on gestation_weeks (UCG-CHTN-01, UCG-PE-04).

finding: J05's stop reads dm_status only: child on insulin, status blank, glucose 15, well -> PAED-03 same_day 'suspect diabetes' (grid, 8 cells).
why: Consistency with L04.
fix: Use the shared diabetes-context list.
